item.title: Van Der Beek GoFundMe Raises $1.1M+
item.description: A GoFundMe page set up for the family of James Van Der Beek has raised over a million dollars. The page was set up by friends following the “Dawson’s Creek” actor’s death from cancer Wednesday at age 48. The page notes that Van Der Beek’s wife, Kimberly, and their six children face an uncertain future having spent almost everything on James’ medical care.

item.title: US Applications For Jobless Benefits Fall To 227,000 Last Week, Remaining At Recent Healthy Levels
item.description: By MATT OTT AP Business Writer WASHINGTON (AP) — The number of Americans applying for unemployment benefits fell last week, remaining within the historically healthy range of the past few years. Applications for jobless aid for the week ending Feb. 7 fell by 5,000 to 227,000 from the previous week, the Labor Department reported Thursday. item.title: Laser Testing Backed
item.description: There are reports that it was planned testing of an anti-drone laser that shut down El Paso’s airport on Wednesday. Congressman Tony Gonzales says that sort of technology is vitally important, especially at high-profile events like the World Cup. But, at a Capitol Hill hearing, he blasted the rollout. The TSA was not notified of the restriction of airspace above El Paso, which he says is “a problem.”

item.title: Trump Blasts Candidate
item.description: President Trump is making it clear that he does not support a run for Congress in Texas by republican Brandon Herrera. A “cease and desist” letter is ordering him to stop using the president’s image on campaign materials, calling it “deceptive.” Trump has endorsed the incumbent in the race, Congressman Tony Gonzales.

item.title: Data Center Growth
item.description: Texas leads the nation in AI computing capacity, according to a new report, but it has not come without controversy. In suburban Dallas, a push for a pause on new industrial development fell apart when Hood County Commissioners got a threat from GOP lawmakers. County Attorney Matt Mills warned that, even though some don’t like the data centers, trying to stop them will bring lawsuits they cannot afford.
